newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends down on greater supply, slow sales.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends down on greater supply, slow sales.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower on indications of increasing supplies of wheat, slow exports and persistent reminders of keen competition, traders said.
Traders said Memphis-based analytical firm Sparks Companies Friday pegged 1996-97 U.S. wheat production at 2.333 billion bushels, above USDA's forecast in August for 2.249 billion.
Also, there signs continue to point to increasing competition for U.S. wheat exports from the European Union, Australia and Canada.
U.S. export and mill sources this week said the Canadian Wheat Board may be stepping up wheat exports to the United States.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 11,000 contracts, down from 17,004 contracts Thursday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, Rosenthal Collins bought 400 March $5.50 calls and sold 400 December $5.50 calls at 2-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated by the CBOT at 4,000 contracts, down from 4,347 Thursday.
Wheat closed one to 5-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with September down one at $4.46-1/2 a bushel.
